notes: The San Francisco Call's Saturday real-estate pages for 1913, as far as the batches hold the year: curiv_dardanelle_ver01 has 1-15 February and curiv_grimes_ver01 16 July to 8 December, so January, March to mid-July and the last three weeks of December are in neither. 24 Saturdays fall in that span; the real-estate news was found on 22 of them (none identified on 16 and 30 August, when the paper ran ten to twelve pages) and read page by page, 32 OCR pages. The section's own header survives only in February; from July the realty news runs without it on one or two pages among the tract advertising, and was found by its headlines (SALES BY ..., leasing reports, BUILDING ACTIVITY picture captions). 1913 is after the 1909 renumbering, so the pages print today's numbers and every entry carries extra.record_date. Taken: numbered addresses where the page says something about the building itself - its form and price in a sale, a firm that leased it, a hall, an auction offering - and buildings located by corner, offset or name with their architect, storeys, lot or institution, placed by hand with research/tools/corner.py. Left out at extraction: sellers, buyers, lessors and lessees who are private people, owners named in loan and contract notices, and the buyers in the Sunset and Richmond lot lists.

coverage.remaining: 1913 outside 1-15 February and 16 July-8 December is in neither batch; the batch index in sources/loc-newspapers.md says where to look next. The rest of the 1913 paper - about 2,860 OCR pages across curiv_dardanelle_ver01 and curiv_grimes_ver01, where the fires, the building-permit lists and the news reports sit - is on disk but unread for this batch. The weekly Real Estate Transactions and Building Contracts lists (on 1, 8 February, 19 July, 1 and 8 November, 29 November, 6 December) were read only for entries naming a building by name or an institution; their metes-and-bounds contracts are the next corner.py batch.
coverage.note: 186 numbered-address mentions and 296 corner, offset and architect cues on the 32 pages, merged into 163 passages and read one by one. About 60 of the numbered mentions are advertisers' and real-estate firms' own offices (the Call's weekly guide to real-estate firms alone repeats 15 a week), about 25 are Oakland, Berkeley, Richmond and Marin, and the Sunset, Richmond and Parkside lot-sales lists give lots, not buildings. Not taken: vacant-lot sales, bare leases between private people, savings-bank loans on vacant lots, a robbery at a private apartment, a wedding notice's home address, numbers the OCR destroyed, and the metes-and-bounds transaction lists. 59 findings: 22 at a street number, 37 located by corner, offset or building name; 25 resolved (13 by hand), 34 unresolved; 21 published on 21 pages, 5 of them seeded; 4 declined because the building on the parcel is later than 1913.
